target.title: fix(whatsapp): add listGroupsLive for real-time group directory
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves The WhatsApp channel directory adapter only registered `listGroups` (which reads from the config map `channels.whatsapp.groups`) but did **not** register `listGroupsLive`. The CLI (and other consumers) prefer `listGroupsLive` when available, so users who have active WhatsApp group memberships but an empty config-based groups map would see `No groups found.` from `openclaw directory groups list --channel whatsapp`. Fixes #76722 ## Why This Change Was Made This PR adds `listWhatsAppDirectoryGroupsLive` that fetches groups from the Baileys socket via `groupFetchAllParticipating()`, with graceful fallback to config when the socket is unavailable or throws. The new function is registered in the channel directory adapter. This mirrors the pattern used by Discord/Slack live directory. A follow-up fix (commit `e7ac40ee0e`) adds name-based filtering: live groups were previously filtered by JID only, so `--query "Family"` would not match a group named "Family Chat". Now builds entries first and filters by both JID and subject name. ## User Impact WhatsApp users who have joined groups but haven't manually configured them in `channels.whatsapp.groups` can now see their real group memberships in the directory. No config changes required — the gateway automatically picks up groups from the active WhatsApp Web session. ## Evidence - `pnpm test extensions/whatsapp/src/directory-config.test.ts` — 8/8 passed (6 new tests + 2 existing) - `pnpm tsgo:test` — passed - `pnpm lint:extensions:bundled` — passed - Autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings Behavior addressed: WhatsApp directory `/groups` now returns real group memberships from the WhatsApp Web socket. Real environment tested: Linux, Node 24.13.1, branch `fix/issue-76722-whatsapp-directory-groups-live`, WhatsApp account `+8618907605370`. Exact steps or command run after this patch: 1. Started gateway: `node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway` 2. Injected a temporary probe in `monitor.ts` at the WhatsApp Web connection ready point (after the "Listening for WhatsApp inbound messages" log) to call `listGroupsLive()` and write results to file: ```js import("../directory-config.js").then(async (mod) => { const entries = await mod.listWhatsAppDirectoryGroupsLive({ cfg, accountId: account.accountId, query: null, limit: null, runtime: defaultRuntime, }); const fs = await import("node:fs"); fs.writeFileSync("/tmp/pr-93996-live-groups-proof.json", JSON.stringify(entries, null, 2)); }).catch(() => {}); ``` 3. Probe was removed after evidence collection. Evidence after fix (gateway log): ``` whatsapp: [default] starting provider (+8618907605370) gateway: ready whatsapp: Listening for WhatsApp inbound messages (DM + all groups; sender allowlist configured). ``` Evidence after fix (live groups returned, `/tmp/pr-93996-live-groups-proof.json`): ```json [ { "kind": "group", "id": "120363409866058990@g.us", "name": "openclaw_test" }, { "kind": "group", "id": "120363409260302345@g.us", "name": "General" }, { "kind": "group", "id": "120363408822325057@g.us", "name": "openclaw_test" }, { "kind": "group", "id": "120363408212902124@g.us", "name": "test_group" } ] ``` Observed result after fix: 4 groups returned from Baileys `groupFetchAllParticipating()`. WhatsApp phone app shows 3 groups — `openclaw_test` (Community), `General`, `test_group`. The API returns 4 entries because `openclaw_test` is a WhatsApp Community, which is represented in the Baileys socket as two separate group JIDs: the announcement group (`120363409866058990@g.us`) and a sub-group (`120363408822325057@g.us`). The WhatsApp app collapses them into one Community entry in the UI. `groupFetchAllParticipating()` returns raw group JIDs without UI-level folding, which is the expected protocol-level behavior. > **🖼️ shows 3 groups: `openclaw_test` (Community), `General`, `test_group` What was not tested: Live E2E with query filtering; Crabbox cross-platform proof.
